transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ethan Ross (Redwood SE); Raj Patel (CTO); Sofia Morales (ML Eng); Liam O'Connor (DevOps); Aisha Brown (PM)

Auto-summary (auto):
Customer is evaluating migration off a mixed stack (OpenAI for chat/embeddings, self-hosted vLLM for some internal workloads) into a single platform. Primary concerns: latency at 99th pct, cost per 1k tokens, eval parity for quality/regression, VPC/KMS and audit logs for compliance. They are interested in Hosted first, then Dedicated or Private depending on data residency and SLA needs.

Topics: migration path, vLLM/TGI compatibility, eval parity, caching/kv cache, quantization tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted, security (SOC2/KMS/SSO), next steps for benchmarks

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everybody thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, i work with customers on migrations and pricing. ethan our se is here too. how's everyone doing?
[00:20] Raj (Monolith CTO): good, thanks. quick heads up we'll probably have to hop off for a minute around the 30 mark if a conflict pops.
[00:28] Maya: totally fine. quick go-round on roles? raj you're the cto, sofia is your ml lead?
[00:34] Sofia (ML Eng): yeah that's right, i'm leading model infra and evals.
[00:38] Liam (DevOps): i'm ops, i manage cloud infra and networking.
[00:42] Aisha (PM): aisha, program manager.
[00:44] Ethan (Redwood SE): great, thanks. we'll aim to cover migration approaches, compatibility concerns—especially around v l l m and T G I models—and then go into hosting options and security.

[02:05] Raj: quick context—we currently call OpenAI for customer-facing chat (gpt-type endpoints) and use embeddings there. For some internal tasks we experimented with a self-hosted vllm setup (vLLM) primarily for cost reasons, but it's fragmented. we're trying to consolidate so we can have consistent evals and observability.

[03:10] Maya: makes sense. high level, teams usually pick two paths: start hosted with Redwood's API to shorten time to value, and then either keep hosted or move to Dedicated reserved capacity as traffic grows or data residency is required. Private (VPC/on-prem) is more for regs. what are your must-haves in the next 3 months?

[03:42] Raj: must-haves: parity on our critical prompts (we have a set of ~40), embedding similarity must be within a tight delta vs OpenAI's embeddings, and 99th percentile latency under 400ms for customer chat. also want to keep costs below our current blended average — which is a little fuzzy because of mixing providers.

[04:20] Sofia: also, we have some models compiled/customized for TGI runtime, and we host some smaller models via v l l m on our 4xA100 nodes. compatibility there is a question — can Redwood serve our TGI-optimized models or do we need to recompile?

[04:58] Ethan: good callout. short answer: we support models exported in standard formats and we have adapters for TGI and v l l m artifacts in many cases. there are sometimes kernel or quantization differences that change perf/quality and we document those per-model. for TGI, often it's a matter of mapping runtime configs; for vllm snapshots we can usually ingest weight formats but we may recommend a small conversion step.

[06:30] Liam: network & security: for Dedicated or Private we'd need VPC peering, our KMS (we use AWS KMS with external key policies), and want to ensure audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. can you do that with hosted?

[06:52] Maya: yes, hosted customers can get audit logs and we have KMS integrations via customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private. Hosted with stricter data residency needs might push you to Dedicated or Private. we can provide a SOC2 report and security whitepaper — i'll attach after the call.

[08:05] Raj: two practical questions: 1) how do you handle prefix caching and kv cache between requests to reduce token cost? 2) will our evals transfer—i mean, do you preserve generation randomness so we can run A/Bs and regression tests?

[08:32] Ethan: for caching we have automatic prefix caching and optional persistent KV cache that you can enable per-route. that reduces repeated context cost for multi-turn flows. regarding eval parity we recommend you use our eval harness; we preserve deterministic sampling settings when requested—also you can pin model versions to ensure repeatability for regression suites. randomness is controllable via temperature/seeds.

[10:12] Sofia: on embeddings — OpenAI's embedding dimension and encoder are, well, opaque; we've been using their ada-embeddings. can we reproduce vector similarity with your curated open models or do we have to keep using OpenAI?

[10:36] Ethan: embeddings are model-specific, you won't get bitwise identical vectors if you switch models. we provide recommended open models with quality profiles and they have similarity deltas documented. usually customers re-run a small sample and we show the delta & downstream impact on search/recall. sometimes you need a tiny reindex or a hybrid approach (keep OpenAI embeddings for older data while generating new ones with the new model).

[12:05] Raj: cost tradeoff question — for heavy inference we saw cheaper token cost with our v l l m self-host vs OpenAI; does Redwood give discounting for dedicated reserved capacity? and can batching/quant help reduce ops latency impact?

[12:36] Maya: yes, Dedicated is reserved pricing with committed throughput discounts and burst policies. Redwood Optimize suggests batching and quantization profiles based on your workload; that can materially reduce per-token compute and cost. we also have auto-batching that respects latency SLOs.

[13:20] Aisha: timeline: we'd like to run a 3-week pilot starting early december to test parity and perf. can you support that?

[13:33] Maya: absolutely. a pilot typically includes a small dedicated test harness or hosted sandbox, integration of your prompts and evals, and a joint benchmark plan. ethan, do you want to summarize the pilot plan?

[13:45] Ethan: sure — step 1: customer uploads canonical prompts & traffic profile; step 2: we run correctness/regression tests (eval parity) and collect latency/throughput metrics; step 3: iterate on batching/kv cache/quant profiles; step 4: share results and recommend hosted vs dedicated. we aim for concrete pass/fail criteria for the 40 critical prompts.

[15:20] Raj: sounds good. one tricky area — some of our prompts rely on custom tool-calling patterns and structured function outputs. does your streaming & function-calling behavior match OpenAI's? we've had subtle differences that break our client-side parser.

[15:45] Ethan: we have a function-calling compatibility layer and streaming mode, but there are subtle shaped-response differences sometimes. part of the pilot is running those exact tool-calls and confirming response shape and content. we also support structured outputs via json-schema hints which helps keep parity.

[17:10] Sofia: on quantization — we've experimented with 4-bit quant on vLLM and saw a small quality drop for the hallucination-sensitive prompts. do you test those tradeoffs?

[17:28] Ethan: yes, our Optimize tool provides model-by-workload quant profiles. we'll run the critical prompt set across full precision and quantized variants, measure regression, and recommend thresholds. sometimes mixed precision or selective quantization per-layer helps.

[19:05] Liam: networking follow-up — if we pick Dedicated, what's the peering window and maintenance impact? our app team requires a predictable update window.

[19:28] Maya: Dedicated customers get a maintenance calendar and we support configurable maintenance windows for minimal disruption. peering can be scheduled during off-hours and we offer fallbacks to Hosted in extreme outage scenarios.

[21:02] Raj: who else from Redwood will be hands-on during pilot? i'd like direct SE support and an escalation contact.

[21:15] Maya: ethan will lead the SE work, and i'll be your AE and point for commercial questions. we'll also assign a solutions engineer for the pilot runbook. we'll include on-call escalation contacts in the SOW.

[22:02] Aisha: about compliance — we need to present to info sec a list of controls mapping to SOC2 and our internal checklist. can you provide a mapping doc?

[22:22] Maya: yes i will attach a controls mapping to SOC2, and include our KMS/SSO docs. also we can provide an architecture whiteboard for how a VPC/private deployment looks.

[24:10] Raj: okay, let's talk concrete numbers — what's typical latency for 7B and 13B models on Dedicated under 8k token lengths? we've been seeing 95-100 ms median on our small nodes but p99 spikes are what worry us.

[24:37] Ethan: approximate numbers: on our Dedicated pool with optimized kernels, 7B medians are ~40-60ms for single-turn short prompts, 13B is ~80-140ms depending on tokenizer and sequence. p99 depends a lot on batching and KV cache hits — with caching you can reduce p99 significantly for multi-turn. we'll include actual numbers from the pilot.

[26:04] Sofia: any gotchas moving from TGI runtime? we have some custom ops compiled into kernels — is recompile required?

[26:25] Ethan: sometimes custom ops need rework; we try to preserve semantics but we may recommend a small integration pass. it's rare for basic models but higher if you use nonstandard layers/kernels. we can run a compatibility scan with your model artifacts during the pilot.

[28:00] Raj: legal & procurement — hosting contract length and termination terms? also data egress charges?

[28:20] Maya: for Dedicated we do 12/24/36 month commits with SLAs. Hosted is month-to-month but with usage terms. egress is generally cloud provider fees; we can show an estimate. we'll have standard enterprise contract terms and we can provide redlines up front.

[30:05] (brief interruption, Raj steps away for 3 minutes)
[33:10] Raj (returning): sorry about that.
[33:15] Aisha: one more product question — how do you surface per-token cost and disputes? our finance team needs token-level billing visibility.

[33:32] Maya: Redwood Console has token-level breakdowns by route/model, and you can export cost reports. we also provide sample throttles and quota alerts.

[34:55] Sofia: we also use multi-turn context windows heavily with large KV cache sizes — how is cache eviction handled and how does it interact with privacy?

[35:15] Ethan: cache eviction is policy-driven; you can configure TTLs and LRU behavior. for privacy, cached content can be stored encrypted and subject to your KMS. with Private deployments you retain full control over cache storage.

[36:40] Liam: what about observability — we want traces tied to requests and per-token latency heatmaps. can we get that?

[36:52] Ethan: yes console has per-request traces and token-level latency breakdowns. you can also instrument with our tracing hooks and export to external tracing backends.

[38:10] Raj: lastly, would you be able to run a quick quality check on our 10-high-priority prompts and give a rough parity score this week?

[38:28] Ethan: yes, if you upload them now or to the sheet we'll queue a small smoke test on Hosted and share a short report.

[39:05] Aisha: we'll upload by end of day.

[39:20] Maya: excellent. recapping next steps: we'll share SOC2 and security docs, provide pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated, Ethan will provision a small test harness for pilot metrics, and you (raj team) will upload prompts and traffic profile.

[40:02] Raj: any blockers on your side?

[40:08] Ethan: none, we just need artifacts and an agreed benchmark plan.

[41:15] Sofia: any guidance on how many tokens/sec we should expect in the pilot with 4 concurrent streams?

[41:28] Ethan: we'll size that in the benchmark template; rough rule-of-thumb: a single A100-equivalent server can do X tokens/s for 13B depending on batching; we'll fill exact numbers once we see seq lengths.

[43:00] Liam: ops question — if we run Dedicated in our cloud region, can you still route failover to Hosted in other regions automatically?

[43:18] Maya: yes, smart routing policies allow failover by policy; we can configure automatic fallback to Hosted or another region's Dedicated pool.

[45:02] Raj: ok, thanks everyone. any final thoughts?

[45:12] Ethan: we'll start the test harness and send the Google sheet link in the chat.
[45:20] Maya: i'll email pricing and security pack after this call and schedule the pilot kickoff for early december pending your artifacts.
[45:34] Aisha: great, thanks.
[46:00] Raj: thanks all.
[47:30] (call ends)
